description: Job Description At Pencil, we are driving innovation in advertising technology through our state-of-the-art SaaS product, which harnesses Generative AI to redefine content creation. Our mission is to make AI the default in advertising without replacing creative people. To achieve this, we need to make sure that our technology isn’t just in the hands of big brands - we need to try to help small businesses and creative individuals too. We're looking for a Security & Trust Specialist to join Pencil at a pivotal moment of growth. This is a hands-on, technical role for someone with a background in desktop support, IT systems administration or a similar technical operations role who is now building a career in security. You'll own the day-to-day security operations that keep Pencil safe — endpoints, identity and access, cloud and SaaS security — and you're happy to lend a hand with practical IT and device issues where needed. You'll work directly with our Head of Security & Trust, who will support your growth into the audit, compliance and vendor-risk side of the role over time. Key responsibilities: Administer and secure endpoints (MDM/Intune, patching, encryption, device compliance), and be willing to pitch in on practical desktop support and device issues when the team needs a hand. Own day-to-day identity and access management — joiner/mover/leaver processes, least-privilege access and quarterly access reviews across Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, GCP and other SaaS tools. Monitor security alerts and logs, escalate promptly, and help investigate and document security events (suspicious logins, compromised credentials, device loss, cloud misconfiguration). Support compliance evidence collection in Vanta for SOC 2, ISO 27001 and ISO 42001, working alongside the Head of Security & Trust rather than owning audit strategy yourself. Help gather evidence for vendor and customer security questionnaires, and flag anything that needs escalating. Identify and implement practical improvements to monitoring, alerting and access control across cloud and endpoint tooling. Your background: A background in desktop support, IT systems administration or a similar technical operations role, now moving into (or already doing blended IT/security) work. Hands-on experience with endpoint management (Intune or similar MDM) and Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 administration. Comfortable with cloud basics (GCP, AWS or Azure IAM) — you don't need deep cloud engineering experience, but you're curious and capable of learning fast. Some exposure to compliance or audit evidence gathering (Vanta or similar) is a bonus, not required. A security certification such as CompTIA Security+, ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity or Microsoft SC-900 — or clear evidence of self-directed learning if you don't have one yet. A genuinely helpful, practical approach — you don't mind switching between security work and helping a colleague with their laptop. You’ll Thrive Here If You… You enjoy being hands-on and don't mind switching between strategic security work and practical, in-the-moment IT problems (Human). You're hungry to grow a career in security and want to learn from the audits and questionnaires you'll be exposed to (Owners). You take ownership of problems end-to-end and don't wait to be told what to do (Owners). You can explain technical issues simply to non-technical colleagues (Simple). KPIs & Success Measures Access reviews and joiner/mover/leaver tasks completed within SLA, with zero access-control audit findings. Endpoint compliance rate (encryption, patching, MDM enrolment) across the device fleet. Time-to-close on security incidents and IT/device issues you support. Quality and completeness of evidence you contribute to Vanta and vendor reviews. Benefits: 25 days PTO plus public holidays, although we operate a Flexible Time Off scheme Health insurance / private medical cover Monthly stipend towards wellness, fitness, and learning and development Remote - work from anywhere in your home country Enhanced parental leave policies, whether you become a parent through birth, adoption or surrogacy Access to our Pencil office in The Shard, London for UK employees Flexible working hours Deep Dive About Pencil Pencil uses AI to make ads. Our mission is to make marketing effective and effortless. We want to become the default way ads get made - because AI ads are 10x faster and cheaper to make, and 2x better performing, than making them without AI. We’re called Pencil because we believe AI will be a tool for creative people, not a replacement - it may even be as fundamental a tool in the future as the pencil was in the past. Pencil was founded in 2018 with a team from Google, Facebook and Uber with backing from Sequoia and Entrepreneur First. We were acquired by The Brandtech Group in 2023 to pursue a shared vision of bringing GenAI to the Fortune 500. https://www.trypencil.com About The Brandtech Group The Brandtech Group’s mission is to be the best company in the world at helping leading global brands drive growth by connecting content, data and media using technology. It was renamed The Brandtech Group in January 2022. Today it generates more than $1BN in revenue and is the largest global digital content partner for many of the world's biggest brands and companies, often using its unique in-housing model. It works with eight of the world's top 10 global advertisers and 49 of the world's top 100. raw.description:
Job Description

At Pencil, we are driving innovation in advertising technology through our state-of-the-art SaaS product, which harnesses Generative AI to redefine content creation. Our mission is to make AI the default in advertising without replacing creative people. To achieve this, we need to make sure that our technology isn’t just in the hands of big brands - we need to try to help small businesses and creative individuals too.

We're looking for a Security & Trust Specialist to join Pencil at a pivotal moment of growth. This is a hands-on, technical role for someone with a background in desktop support, IT systems administration or a similar technical operations role who is now building a career in security. You'll own the day-to-day security operations that keep Pencil safe — endpoints, identity and access, cloud and SaaS security — and you're happy to lend a hand with practical IT and device issues where needed. You'll work directly with our Head of Security & Trust, who will support your growth into the audit, compliance and vendor-risk side of the role over time.

Key responsibilities:

  • Administer and secure endpoints (MDM/Intune, patching, encryption, device compliance), and be willing to pitch in on practical desktop support and device issues when the team needs a hand.

  • Own day-to-day identity and access management — joiner/mover/leaver processes, least-privilege access and quarterly access reviews across Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, GCP and other SaaS tools.

  • Monitor security alerts and logs, escalate promptly, and help investigate and document security events (suspicious logins, compromised credentials, device loss, cloud misconfiguration).

  • Support compliance evidence collection in Vanta for SOC 2, ISO 27001 and ISO 42001, working alongside the Head of Security & Trust rather than owning audit strategy yourself.

  • Help gather evidence for vendor and customer security questionnaires, and flag anything that needs escalating.

  • Identify and implement practical improvements to monitoring, alerting and access control across cloud and endpoint tooling.

Your background:

  • A background in desktop support, IT systems administration or a similar technical operations role, now moving into (or already doing blended IT/security) work.

  • Hands-on experience with endpoint management (Intune or similar MDM) and Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 administration.

  • Comfortable with cloud basics (GCP, AWS or Azure IAM) — you don't need deep cloud engineering experience, but you're curious and capable of learning fast.

  • Some exposure to compliance or audit evidence gathering (Vanta or similar) is a bonus, not required.

  • A security certification such as CompTIA Security+, ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity or Microsoft SC-900 — or clear evidence of self-directed learning if you don't have one yet.

  • A genuinely helpful, practical approach — you don't mind switching between security work and helping a colleague with their laptop.

You’ll Thrive Here If You…

  • You enjoy being hands-on and don't mind switching between strategic security work and practical, in-the-moment IT problems (Human).

  • You're hungry to grow a career in security and want to learn from the audits and questionnaires you'll be exposed to (Owners).

  • You take ownership of problems end-to-end and don't wait to be told what to do (Owners).

  • You can explain technical issues simply to non-technical colleagues (Simple).

 

KPIs & Success Measures

  • Access reviews and joiner/mover/leaver tasks completed within SLA, with zero access-control audit findings.

  • Endpoint compliance rate (encryption, patching, MDM enrolment) across the device fleet.

  • Time-to-close on security incidents and IT/device issues you support.

  • Quality and completeness of evidence you contribute to Vanta and vendor reviews.

  • Access to our Pencil office in The Shard, London for UK employees

  • Flexible working hours

Pencil uses AI to make ads. Our mission is to make marketing effective and effortless. We want to become the default way ads get made - because AI ads are 10x faster and cheaper to make, and 2x better performing, than making them without AI.

At Unmind, we're here to create better mental health.

We believe mental health should be a source of strength, not struggle – for people, teams, and entire organisations.

Now we’re looking for more brilliant people to help us do it.

🚀 Our Values

We’re building a company where ambition and empathy go hand in hand.

Outpace the rest – Move fast. Deliver excellence.

Stronger together – We go further, faster, together.

Client first – We win, when our clients win.

If you need adjustments during the process, tell us when you apply or email Learn more about how we hire and our commitment to equity in our Candidate FAQ →

🎯 The Role — Senior Talent Partner

This isn't a pure talent acquisition role, and we think that's what makes it interesting.
We're a Series C business of around 90 people, with a small, hands-on People team. As our Senior Talent Partner, you'll own end-to-end hiring across the whole business - this includes Engineering, Product and Design – but you'll also hire for our Commercial teams (Sales, Client Success, Marketing) and head office functions like Finance and People.

Roughly 80% of your time will be talent acquisition. The rest goes into the wider employee experience: benchmarking salaries, running our remote onboarding sessions and helping to drive culture initiatives like our Culture Champions network.

Priorities shift quickly at our stage. One week you might be closing a senior software engineer and a sales hire at the same time; the next you're benchmarking a promotion and welcoming a new cohort of Unminders. If you like variety, enjoy working closely with leaders and want to shape how a growing company hires and welcomes its people, this role is for you.

Talent:

  • Culture initiatives - Support our Culture Champions to keep connection and culture strong in a remote-first company. Help plan and run initiatives that bring our values to life.

title: Senior Android Computer Vision Engineer
description: Senior Android Computer Vision Engineer Location: Budapest, Hungary Ways of working: Hybrid Contract: Permanent, full-time About Hawk-Eye Innovations Hawk-Eye Innovations is at the forefront of sports technology, delivering officiating, tracking, broadcast and performance solutions across some of the world's biggest sports. As part of Sony Sports, we continue to push the boundaries of innovation, helping athletes, coaches, teams, broadcasters and governing bodies make better decisions through technology. Bring computer vision to the world of sport What if athletes, coaches and teams could access the kind of tracking technology that has traditionally been out of reach? We’re building a new generation of tracking services for elite and semi-professional sport, putting powerful computer vision technology directly into the hands of the people who need it most. We’re looking for a Senior Android Computer Vision Engineer to help make that possible. You’ll join a small, cross-functional engineering team building products at the cutting edge of sport and technology. With the direction set and plenty still to be built, you’ll have the autonomy to shape solutions, make important technical decisions and see your work make a real difference. The role You’ll own computer vision on the device, taking detection and tracking models and making them work reliably on consumer Android phones and tablets. That means much more than getting a model to run. You’ll optimise and profile inference for real-world hardware, balancing performance with accuracy across different devices, lighting conditions and environments. You’ll work close to the camera capture pipeline, where frame timing, exposure and device behaviour can all affect the quality of the output. Your challenge is to ensure that the data produced on a mobile device is accurate, reliable and trusted by the wider tracking system. You’ll work closely with mobile, backend, computer vision and machine learning engineers, with the freedom to own both your technical approach and its implementation. We also embrace AI-augmented and AI-delegated development as part of how we work, enabling a small team to build and iterate at pace. This is an opportunity to solve genuinely challenging engineering problems, influence how on-device vision is built and help establish the foundations for a technology that can change how sport is experienced and analysed. What you’ll be doing Own on-device inference: Design and implement Android inference solutions that meet demanding accuracy, latency and performance requirements. Build the native Android vision layer: Develop and maintain C++ components using the Android NDK, alongside JNI bindings that connect them to our Kotlin application. Optimise models for mobile: Convert, quantise, profile and optimise detection and tracking models, exploring techniques such as pruning, graph optimisation and operator-level improvements. Solve real-world camera challenges: Work close to the capture pipeline, understanding how frame timing, exposure and camera behaviour influence model performance. Make accuracy measurable: Build validation tools and measurement processes that demonstrate performance against ground truth in real-world conditions. Engineer for real devices: Account for thermal constraints, battery consumption, hardware differences and the unpredictable conditions encountered in the field. Collaborate on model improvements: Work with our computer vision and machine learning specialists to identify, prototype and evaluate improvements to model performance. Shape technical decisions: Help determine what should run on-device and what should run elsewhere, bringing clear reasoning and an understanding of technical trade-offs. Build production-quality software: Write maintainable, testable and reliable code that meets the team's engineering standards. Work across disciplines: Communicate clearly with mobile application, backend and machine learning engineers who depend on your work. Build with AI: Use AI-assisted and delegated development tools as a standard part of your workflow, working within our security and intellectual property guidelines. As the team grows, there may also be opportunities to mentor other engineers, take technical leadership of on-device vision and establish the standards and practices that shape our approach to edge AI. What you’ll bring You’re an experienced computer vision or machine learning engineer who enjoys taking algorithms beyond the lab and making them work reliably in production. You’re comfortable working close to the hardware, investigating problems that don’t show up in controlled environments and making informed trade-offs between accuracy, performance and resource consumption. You can work independently, communicate your thinking clearly and collaborate with engineers across different disciplines. You’ll ideally bring: At least 4 years of applied computer vision or machine learning engineering experience , including solutions deployed into production. About Hawk-Eye Innovations

Hawk-Eye Innovations is at the forefront of sports technology, delivering officiating, tracking, broadcast and performance solutions across some of the world's biggest sports. As part of Sony Sports, we continue to push the boundaries of innovation, helping athletes, coaches, teams, broadcasters and governing bodies make better decisions through technology.

Bring computer vision to the world of sport

What if athletes, coaches and teams could access the kind of tracking technology that has traditionally been out of reach?

We’re building a new generation of tracking services for elite and semi-professional sport, putting powerful computer vision technology directly into the hands of the people who need it most.

We’re looking for a Senior Android Computer Vision Engineer to help make that possible.

You’ll join a small, cross-functional engineering team building products at the cutting edge of sport and technology. With the direction set and plenty still to be built, you’ll have the autonomy to shape solutions, make important technical decisions and see your work make a real difference.

The role

You’ll own computer vision on the device, taking detection and tracking models and making them work reliably on consumer Android phones and tablets.

That means much more than getting a model to run. You’ll optimise and profile inference for real-world hardware, balancing performance with accuracy across different devices, lighting conditions and environments. You’ll work close to the camera capture pipeline, where frame timing, exposure and device behaviour can all affect the quality of the output.

Your challenge is to ensure that the data produced on a mobile device is accurate, reliable and trusted by the wider tracking system.

You’ll work closely with mobile, backend, computer vision and machine learning engineers, with the freedom to own both your technical approach and its implementation. We also embrace AI-augmented and AI-delegated development as part of how we work, enabling a small team to build and iterate at pace.

This is an opportunity to solve genuinely challenging engineering problems, influence how on-device vision is built and help establish the foundations for a technology that can change how sport is experienced and analysed.

What you’ll be doing

  • Own on-device inference: Design and implement Android inference solutions that meet demanding accuracy, latency and performance requirements.

  • Build the native Android vision layer: Develop and maintain C++ components using the Android NDK, alongside JNI bindings that connect them to our Kotlin application.

  • Optimise models for mobile: Convert, quantise, profile and optimise detection and tracking models, exploring techniques such as pruning, graph optimisation and operator-level improvements.

  • Solve real-world camera challenges: Work close to the capture pipeline, understanding how frame timing, exposure and camera behaviour influence model performance.

  • Make accuracy measurable: Build validation tools and measurement processes that demonstrate performance against ground truth in real-world conditions.

  • Engineer for real devices: Account for thermal constraints, battery consumption, hardware differences and the unpredictable conditions encountered in the field.

  • Collaborate on model improvements: Work with our computer vision and machine learning specialists to identify, prototype and evaluate improvements to model performance.

  • Shape technical decisions: Help determine what should run on-device and what should run elsewhere, bringing clear reasoning and an understanding of technical trade-offs.

  • Build production-quality software: Write maintainable, testable and reliable code that meets the team's engineering standards.

  • Work across disciplines: Communicate clearly with mobile application, backend and machine learning engineers who depend on your work.

  • Build with AI: Use AI-assisted and delegated development tools as a standard part of your workflow, working within our security and intellectual property guidelines.

As the team grows, there may also be opportunities to mentor other engineers, take technical leadership of on-device vision and establish the standards and practices that shape our approach to edge AI.

What you’ll bring

You’re an experienced computer vision or machine learning engineer who enjoys taking algorithms beyond the lab and making them work reliably in production.

You’re comfortable working close to the hardware, investigating problems that don’t show up in controlled environments and making informed trade-offs between accuracy, performance and resource consumption. You can work independently, communicate your thinking clearly and collaborate with engineers across different disciplines.

You’ll ideally bring:

  • At least 4 years of applied computer vision or machine learning engineering experience, including solutions deployed into production.

  • Demonstrable experience running inference on Android or embedded devices, rather than working exclusively with desktop or server hardware.

  • A degree in computer science, engineering, mathematics or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

  • A strong interest in learning new technologies, tools and platforms.

Experience in automotive, embedded systems or other resource-constrained environments could be particularly relevant.

Technical skills

You’ll have expert-level knowledge of:

  • Applied computer vision, including object detection, tracking, camera geometry and the challenges that arise outside controlled environments.

  • Mobile or embedded inference runtimes, including model conversion and quantisation toolchains.

  • Model optimisation and performance profiling for resource-constrained hardware.

  • C++, particularly the Android NDK and JNI.

  • Measuring and validating model accuracy against ground truth.

You’ll also be comfortable with:

  • Kotlin, with enough experience to work effectively across the JNI boundary.

  • Python for prototyping, tooling and data analysis.

  • Mobile camera capture pipelines, including frame timing and exposure control.

  • Machine learning fundamentals, allowing you to contribute meaningfully to discussions about model improvements.

  • Git, code reviews and continuous integration practices.

It would be beneficial to understand:

  • Real-time and latency-sensitive systems.

  • Spatial computing and multi-view reconstruction.

  • The Android application development and release lifecycle.

You don’t need to have worked with every technology listed. We’re interested in the depth of your engineering experience, your ability to solve difficult problems and your willingness to learn.

Our technology

Our stack includes C++, Android NDK, JNI, Kotlin, Python and AWS, supported by Git, GitHub Actions, Jira and Android mobile inference and profiling tools.

Why Hawk-Eye?

At Hawk-Eye, you'll have the opportunity to work on technology used across the world's leading sports while solving complex technical challenges alongside talented engineers and product teams. You'll play a key role in shaping products from the ground up, working in an environment that values innovation, collaboration and continuous learning.

If you're excited by the opportunity to build cutting-edge mobile products that make a genuine impact in sport, we'd love to hear from you.

The role

We're looking for a People Operations Lead to set the standard for how People Ops runs in Belfast, and to own the workplace experience in our Belfast office. You'll be the senior specialist responsible for compliance, policy, process design and strategic projects, and the person who makes sure the Belfast team has a workplace that supports how they do their best work.

This is a senior individual contributor role not a people manager. You'll report to the People Operations Manager and partner closely with our London People Operations Lead, London Workplace Manager, and with Talent, People Partners, Legal and Finance. You'll set the standard for operational excellence across the team and be the People and Workplace face of 9fin in Belfast.

What you'll own

  • Operational excellence in Belfast: Own the day-to-day running of People Operations for our Belfast population. Set the bar for accuracy, timeliness and employee experience across the full lifecycle - joiners, leavers, changes, probation, right-to-work, background screening, leave and absence.

  • Compliance & audit-readiness: Keep 9fin compliant with UK employment law, statutory requirements and internal audit standards. Maintain audit-ready records, run periodic control checks, and flag risks early. Partner with Legal to interpret and apply changes in employment law.

  • Policy & handbook: Own the Northern Ireland policy set - the NI-specific policies, handbook annexes and local variations that reflect how employment law and practice differ here. Contribute to the wider UK handbook alongside the London Lead, and make sure Belfast-specific guidance is clear, current and used.

  • Strategic project leadership: Own one or two of the biggest People Ops projects each cycle end-to-end - scoping the problem, aligning stakeholders, delivering the work, and measuring the impact. Think workplace improvements, early careers outreach, benefits redesign.

  • Workflows & automations: Design and build the workflows and automations that reduce manual work across the lifecycle. Identify what should be templated, what should be automated, and what should be redesigned entirely. Ship the improved version.

  • Belfast workplace ownership: Own the workplace experience in the Belfast office end-to-end - office operations, facilities and supplier relationships, health and safety, in-office events, hybrid working experience, and joiner day one logistics. Partner with the London Workplace Manager on standards, budget and consistency across offices.

  • Complex casework: Working closely with the People Partners, handling the trickiest Belfast people situations - complex leave, contract variations, sensitive investigations support - with strong judgment on risk, employee experience and commercial context.

  • People data & insight: Build the reporting and dashboards leadership actually uses. Present operational recommendations backed by data to the People Operations Manager, Head of People and wider business.

  • Budget partnership: Support the People Operations Manager on Belfast sub-team budget - scoping future spend, analysing current spend, articulating ROI, and making recommendations.

What you'll bring

  • 5+ years in People Operations / HR Operations in a scaling company, with meaningful ownership of both process design and hands-on delivery.

  • Deep working knowledge of UK employment law and compliance - you're the person others check with before making a call.

  • Strong track record of writing and rolling out policies that hold up in practice.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead People Ops projects end-to-end - scoping, stakeholder alignment, delivery, measurement.

  • Comfort designing workflows and automations that meaningfully reduce manual work.

  • Experience owning workplace, office or facilities operations - or a clear appetite to add this to your remit and do it well.

  • Exceptional attention to detail. You catch the thing others miss, and you build systems that catch it next time.

  • Comfortable being the "go-to" person: briefs seniors, unblocks peers, and represents the People and Workplace function credibly in cross-functional forums.

  • Bias to build: you would rather design the process than inherit one.

Nice to have

  • Prior experience at a scaling fintech, capital markets business, or high-growth B2B SaaS.

  • Familiarity with SOC 2 / ISO People-related controls and audit prep.

  • Experience building automations across the People Tech stack, including the HRIS.

  • Prior workplace, facilities, health and safety, or office management experience.

What success looks like in your first 12 months

  • Belfast operations run predictably and to a high standard, with clean handoffs across Finance, IT and Workplace.

  • Compliance is demonstrably audit-ready; the handbook and policy set are current, well-drafted, and used.

  • At least two major strategic project shipped end-to-end.

  • Workflows and automations have visibly reduced manual work across the lifecycle.

  • The Belfast office runs smoothly - the team notices the workplace, in a good way.

  • You're the person the business escalates the hard Belfast people-ops questions to - and the answers hold up.

Our benefits

We’re a scaling start up, and we enjoy sharing our success, when the company succeeds, we always reinvest that in our people. We also offer huge amounts of responsibility, an abundance of opportunity for growth and a platform to truly excel.

 

Financial & Insurance

  • Competitive Salary (our salary bands are benchmarked at the top end of the market)

  • Equity options

  • Pension (your minimum contributions are 4% with 9fin matching up to 7%)

  • Private Medical Insurance

  • Paid sick leave with Income Protection for long periods of illness

  • Group Life Assurance

  • Season Ticket Loan & Cycle to Work schemes

Time off

  • 25 holiday days per year

  • Local public holidays (with the ability to exchange them for alternative days)

  • Work abroad for up to 3 months a year

  • 1 month paid sabbatical after 5 years of service

  • Enhanced parental leave & flexible working arrangements available

Growth & Culture

  • Professional learning and development budget

  • Quarterly team socials

  • Summer and Winter company social events

Location
9fin is a hybrid company, and the office is a regular part of how we work. From January 2027, all employees will work from their designated 9fin office on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Some teams may be asked to be in the office more often, where the nature of their work calls for it. For the rest of the week, you may work from wherever works best for you and your team

9fin is an equal opportunities employer

At 9fin we are dedicated to building and promoting a fair and inclusive workplace where everyone can reach their full potential and truly belong. We recognize that building diverse teams enables a more creative and productive environment. If you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t perfectly align with the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might just be who we’re looking for — either for this role, or perhaps another.

raw.description:
About Us

Avenir Collective. Building the future of beauty, personal care and lifestyle brands.

We acquire and scale high-potential consumer brands, bringing together the capital, people and operating expertise to turn strong brands into enduring businesses. Our difference is that we are operators, actively managing our brands and providing the capabilities, infrastructure and expertise they need to scale, while preserving the product, purpose and consumer connection that make each brand special.

We’re building a connected house of brands where great people, brands and ideas come together. If you’re excited by building businesses, solving problems and working with a collaborative, entrepreneurial team, we’d love to hear from you.


Your role at a Glance 

 

As a Senior Commercial Finance Manager in our Finance team, you will play a key role in supporting the Group Finance Director and wider leadership team by delivering accurate, timely and insightful financial reporting. Your main focus will be leading the preparation of Group reporting, budgeting and forecasting processes, ensuring financial information is clear, meaningful and supports better business decisions through close collaboration with stakeholders across the organisation.

This role is ideal for someone with strong commercial finance expertise and a proactive, analytical mindset, who enjoys working closely with senior stakeholders and using financial insight to influence business performance. Your work will directly impact how we understand our performance, manage costs and identify opportunities for growth across the business.

Location & Flexibility 

  • Full-time, permanent role based at our modern office in Holborn, London 

  • Working Hours: 40 hours per week, 9 am to 6 pm with a one-hour lunch  

  • This position is hybrid, with the expectation to go to the London office at least 2 or 3 days per week

Key responsibilities

Group Reporting 
• Prepare the Group's monthly management reporting. 
• Produce reporting for the Executive Leadership Team and Board. 
• Analyse revenue, gross margin, operating costs and EBITDA. 
• Prepare clear commentary explaining business performance, key movements, risks and opportunities. 
• Investigate queries from the Group Finance Director and senior leaders, providing clear answers and recommendations. 
• Continue to improve reporting, KPIs and dashboards. 
 
Budgeting and Forecasting 
• Support the forecasting process. 
• Support the annual budget process. 
• Prepare financial models and scenario analysis. 
• Monitor performance against budget and forecast, explaining key variances. 
• Highlight risks and opportunities early. 
 
OPEX Reporting 
• Prepare the Group's operating expense reporting. 
• Work closely with budget holders to review monthly spend. 
• Lead regular meetings with budget holders to review performance and forecasts. 
• Prepare monthly operating expense forecasts. 
• Investigate and explain significant variances. 
• Identify opportunities to improve cost control and reporting. 
 
Business Partnering 
• Build strong relationships with stakeholders across the business. 
• Provide financial support and challenge where needed. 
• Help managers understand their financial performance. 
• Support business cases and commercial decisions with clear financial analysis. 
 
Month End 
• Work with the Financial Control team to ensure accurate month-end reporting. 
• Prepare monthly variance analysis and supporting commentary. 
• Support ad hoc analysis and reporting as required. 
 
Continuous Improvement 
• Improve reporting, forecasting and planning processes. 
• Look for opportunities to automate and simplify reporting. 
• Help improve the quality and consistency of financial information.  

About you

  • ACA, ACCA or CIMA qualified with strong experience in Commercial Finance, FP&A or Finance Business Partnering roles.

  • Proven experience preparing management reporting, budgets, forecasts and financial models in a commercial environment.

  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret complex financial information and translate it into actionable insights.

  • Confident communicator with experience partnering with senior stakeholders and explaining financial concepts to non-finance teams.

  • Advanced Excel skills, with experience using financial systems such as NetSuite and reporting tools such as Power BI desirable.

  • Experience working within consumer products, retail, e-commerce or another fast-paced, high-growth environment.

What Success Looks Like 
 
Within your first six months you will: 

  • Produce accurate and reliable Group reporting. 

  • Deliver high-quality budgets and forecasts. 

  • Build strong relationships with budget holders. 

  • Become the first point of contact for commercial finance reporting and analysis. 

  • Improve the quality and efficiency of reporting. 

  • Provide clear answers and insight that support better business decisions. 

 

Perks & Benefits 

  • Salary: £75,000 to £85,000 per year

  • 30 days holiday + 8 UK bank holidays

  • Pension contribution Scheme – 5% from you, 3% from us.

  • Private Medical Insurance – Includes travel, vision & dental (Vitality)

  • Work from Abroad – One month per year, anywhere in the world

  • Bonus Scheme – Discretionary bonus, based on individual and company performance

  • Mental Health Support – Free, confidential therapy via Spill

  • Opportunity for International Travel – Our team members have been to New York, Vegas, Amsterdam… and Birmingham!

  • Flexi-Fridays – Finish early one Friday per month

raw.description:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Our Global Structure

Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

About the team

Deliveroo connects millions of consumers with the restaurants and brands they love. Our Integrated Marketing team sits at the heart of how we bring those relationships to life — combining customer insight, commercial opportunity and creativity to drive growth for Deliveroo and our partners.

Within Central Integrated Marketing, the Merchant & Ads team sets the global strategy for how we partner with merchants to help them grow on our marketplace and create compelling reasons for consumers to choose Deliveroo. This is an opportunity to shape Deliveroo's global approach to merchant partnerships, building high-impact collaborations with some of the world's most recognised and loved brands. This will be a hybrid role - working 3 days a week from our London HQ. 

About the role

  • Owns the New Verticals merchant and ads marketing strategy end to end, reporting into the Merchant & Ads Integrated Marketing Director.

  • Responsible for the creation and deployment of New Verticals merchant marketing playbooks across co marketing, promotions, and ads.

  • Responsible for the creation and deployment of the New Verticals sell in strategy and associated sell in materials for adoption by local teams.

  • Supports local marketing teams with key enterprise merchant relationships at the global level, and supports local New Verticals marketing initiatives.

What you'll be doing

Ads & Monetization Strategy

  • Own the New Verticals specific ads and monetization strategy across owned and external surfaces, feeding into the global monetization strategy.

  • Lead pricing, packaging, and investment decisions for merchant advertising in your category, in partnership with Commercial and Finance.

Category Playbook: New Verticals

  • Own and evolve the New Verticals merchant marketing playbook, setting how co marketing, promotions, and advertising work for grocery and retail merchants globally.

  • Lead change initiatives that improve how New Verticals merchant marketing works, bringing Local Integrated Marketing and Functional Marketing along with you.

Key Merchant Relationship Management

  • Support local marketing teams with key enterprise merchant relationships at the global level, and support delivery of priority New Verticals marketing initiatives with those merchants.

  • Act as the senior escalation point for merchant issues that cross multiple markets or functions.

Cross Functional Stakeholder Management

  • Serve as the primary marketing partner to Merchant S&O and Commercial for New Verticals, translating category priorities into marketing and ads strategy.

  • Represent New Verticals in cross functional forums, shaping the roadmap for merchant facing and ads facing surfaces.

Sell In Strategy & Sales Enablement

  • Own the sell-in strategy for New Verticals merchant and ads programmes, defining how Commercial and Local teams pitch these programmes to merchants.

  • Oversee the sell in materials, case studies, and proof points for New Verticals, using performance data to continuously refine them.

Central Strategy & Market Coordination

  • Own delivery of the New Verticals merchant marketing goals, coordinating a consistent strategy across all Deliveroo markets.

  • Report on New Verticals merchant and ads marketing performance to senior stakeholders, own specific business metrics, and lead course correction when needed.

Requirements

  • 7+ years of marketing experience, ideally including merchant marketing, retail media, ads, or category marketing in a consumer or marketplace business.

  • Track record of owning the marketing strategy for an entire team or category, and resolving complex delivery challenges that span multiple teams or functions.

  • Experience managing people, and comfortable managing other people managers as your team grows.

  • Strong commercial acumen, seen as a go to expert for merchant or ads marketing, using business and financial data to make sound decisions in ambiguous situations.

  • Confident communicator, able to present complex ideas to large groups and flex your style for directors and department leadership.

  • Skilled at establishing and owning cross functional partnerships, using relationships and creative thinking to work through conflict.

  • Proven ability to lead change initiatives that improve how a team or category works, bringing others along with you.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to synthesise complex, cross functional inputs into a clear plan and narrative.

Why Join Us?

At Deliveroo, you'll do work that matters, solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that's constantly evolving. We're food lovers, problem solvers, community builders and more, brought together by a shared drive to make things better. Working here you can expect to:

🔧 Make a visible impact every day

Your work directly improves experiences for customers, partners and riders.

🌱 Learn fast in an entrepreneurial environment

Work close to the market with autonomy, pace and real responsibility.

🧠 Build a career, not just a role

Stretch yourself, develop new skills and grow as the business evolves.

🌎 Deliver together in an inclusive culture

Collaborative, values-driven teams that support how you work best.

We aim to create a fair process that lets your skills shine—our interview typically includes 3-4 stages. Find more about how we hire here.

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.

If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you'll have the opportunity to let us know once you've submitted your application. We'll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

If you're excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we'd love to hear from you!


Beware of recruitment scams: DASH Brands will never ask you to pay money or share sensitive financial information during hiring — learn more about DASH Brands' legitimate recruiting process at careersatdoordash.com/recruitment-scam-awareness.

title: Communications Lead
description: Who we are Yubo is the Social Discovery app to make new friends and hang out online. By eliminating likes and follows, we empower our users to create genuine connections and show up as their true selves. We've pioneered a new way for Gen Z to socialize online, and with millions of active users, our goal is to redefine how we connect today and tomorrow. Our team is international, multicultural and deeply committed to its mission. As the leading platform to socialize online, we have a special responsibility to build a safe digital space for our community. Safety is embedded in our DNA, and our proactive approach focuses on user protection, support, and education. Join us in this exciting journey and help us shape the future of social interactions! About this role Yubo doesn't have a PR team yet, and that's exactly why this role exists: to build one from scratch and help Yubo become culturally relevant, resilient to reputational bumps, and a real driver of growth. It's a rare chance to shape a PR function from day one inside a fast-moving global tech company. You'll design how it works, lead our agency partner, and craft the stories, moments and relationships that make people pay attention to Yubo. The role covers everyday consumer stories, corporate communications, and handling sensitive issues or crises when they arise. To start, you'll focus on the US, UK and France, with room to grow from there. You'll report to the Director of Brand & Communications and work closely with teams across the business, especially Brand, Product, Data, Trust & Safety and Legal. You'll own the relationship with our PR agency, making sure they feel like a true extension of the team, and you'll help set up the habits and processes that make PR part of how Yubo works day to day. This is a freelance role on a 6-month contract, with a target start in Q4 2026. Your responsibilites Set up how PR works at Yubo Build PR operations and onboard Yubo's PR agency, setting clear ways to spot stories, check facts, and turn insight into coverage. Dig into Yubo's data to find trends and stories worth telling. Build a simple way to report on PR performance, linking coverage and sentiment to awareness and growth. Review and embed Yubo's Crisis Comms Playbook. Plan and run the PR agenda Build Yubo's 2027 PR calendar and strategy, balancing campaigns, cultural moments, and day-to-day press activity. Lead proactive and reactive media relations so Yubo speaks with a clear, consistent voice. Spot and activate cultural moments through PR, research, events, creator partnerships and other earned activity. Team up with Product and Data to build proof points and stories that show what Yubo means to people. Look after Yubo's reputation Advise senior leaders on reputational opportunities and risks. Support corporate communications and reactive issues management when needed. Work with Trust & Safety and Legal so Yubo talks about sensitive topics responsibly. Help rally the right people internally when a crisis hits. Who you are You're a proactive PR lead with sharp cultural instincts and a track record of creating stories that genuinely earn attention, not just promote launches. You'll bring: Solid PR experience, with real results to show from leading a function or campaign. A good read on Gen-Z culture and how 18 to 24 year-olds socialise and engage online. Experience turning insight and data into media stories, including digging into data yourself to find the angle. A track record of using different levers to earn attention: influencers, experts, events, activations, research, stunts. Experience managing and getting the best out of an external PR agency. Good judgement under pressure, with experience in issues or crisis communications. Strong writing and speaking skills, comfortable with both consumer storytelling and sensitive corporate messaging. The ability to influence cross-functional teams and senior stakeholders. A self-starter mindset, with examples of building something from the ground up. Nice to have, but don't let that stop you: Experience in high-growth tech, consumer apps, youth culture, media, entertainment or lifestyle. Experience in the US market, including relationships with US media and journalists. Within a month, you will Get familiar with Yubo's product, mission and community, and where our communications and reputation stand today. Meet key people across Brand, Product, Data, Trust & Safety and Legal. Start onboarding our PR agency and reviewing the Crisis Comms Playbook. Within 3 months, you will Have set up solid working habits with the PR agency and cross-functional teams. Be well into building the 2027 PR strategy, calendar and measurement framework. Have embedded the Crisis Comms Playbook and be actively building relationships with consumer, culture, lifestyle, tech and business media. Within 6 months, you will Have delivered Yubo's finished 2027 PR strategy and calendar. Have landed our first standout data- and culture-led stories in top-tier media, backed by a working way to measure PR performance. Have wrapped up the agency onboarding and defined the role of creators, experts, events and activations in Yubo's communications, leaving a solid foundation for what's next. The recruitment process A first introductory call with Nicolas, Talent Acquisition A case study with Alex, our Brand Director. Our approach to privacy & safety As part of your role, you may handle tools and features involving personal data. We expect all employees to demonstrate strong awareness of privacy and safety issues, and to actively support our Privacy & Safety by Design efforts. Our team is international, multicultural and deeply committed to its mission. As the leading platform to socialize online, we have a special responsibility to build a safe digital space for our community. Safety is embedded in our DNA, and our proactive approach focuses on user protection, support, and education.

Join us in this exciting journey and help us shape the future of social interactions!

About this role

Yubo doesn't have a PR team yet, and that's exactly why this role exists: to build one from scratch and help Yubo become culturally relevant, resilient to reputational bumps, and a real driver of growth.

It's a rare chance to shape a PR function from day one inside a fast-moving global tech company. You'll design how it works, lead our agency partner, and craft the stories, moments and relationships that make people pay attention to Yubo. The role covers everyday consumer stories, corporate communications, and handling sensitive issues or crises when they arise. To start, you'll focus on the US, UK and France, with room to grow from there.

You'll report to the Director of Brand & Communications and work closely with teams across the business, especially Brand, Product, Data, Trust & Safety and Legal. You'll own the relationship with our PR agency, making sure they feel like a true extension of the team, and you'll help set up the habits and processes that make PR part of how Yubo works day to day.

title: Product Designer - Paris
description: As a Product Designer, you'll work on the H Platform, where our users create and run agentic AI workflows powered by our models. Nobody has written the playbook for designing these experiences yet. Our next stage is making the platform truly useful for its users and levelling it up, in design as much as in technology, and you'll build the product experiences that deliver real value in organisations. At H Company, we believe AI should take action in the real world, and our mission is to make agentic AI genuinely useful for large organisations. We're pioneers in computer use: our own vision-language models power agents that see, click and type their way through the software businesses already run, with no integrations or rebuilds, and we own the whole stack, from research and models to the products built on top of them. What you'll be doing Talking to our users constantly to understand their needs and figure out what will make the platform truly useful for them. Turning those insights into research and explorations, looking at problems from different angles before settling on a direction. Picking the right tool for each task: a Figma design, a prototype, or a small PR when a quick change is the fastest way to ship. Testing what you build with users, measuring its impact (A/B testing, user interviews, users daily use data...) and iterating quickly based on what you learn. Shaping the roadmap together with the whole team, engineers and PMs alike. Who you'll work with The role sits in our Product team, which is responsible for product direction, strategy and design. You'll join the product designer who owns design and UX today, and work closely with product, engineering and forward deployed engineers. What we think it takes Above all, we want someone who cares deeply about users, has great product taste and can explain it, moves fast while keeping quality high, leaves their ego at the door and welcomes feedback. Likely a good fit if you Have 5+ years of experience as a Product Designer at tech companies. Have excellent UX, UI and interaction design skills, and can make complex, technical flows, like building and running AI agent workflows, feel simple and intuitive. Have a portfolio that shows your latest work. Have hands-on experience running user tests and A/B tests. Know when a proven solution is good enough and when a problem deserves something new. Have designed complex data or ML/AI-driven products: you know how to make complex systems understandable and how to design for AI behaviour that isn't always predictable, building trust and keeping users in control. Are comfortable in technical discussions: you can dig into constraints and trade-offs with engineers and ramp up quickly on technical topics to discuss them with our researchers and more technical engineers. Are fluent in Figma. Can work within a design system and contribute to it. Stronger still if you Have designed platforms: complex B2B web or desktop software used by professionals, whether that's tools to build and run workflows, big data and analytics software, operational dashboards or other data-dense interfaces. Are curious about code and AI in your design workflow. Every design team is still figuring out how AI changes the way we work, and we're no different, so we'd love someone who has started experimenting, whether by prototyping in code, building small tools or bringing AI into their process, and who wants to keep exploring with us. If you match most of this but not every point, apply anyway. We care far more about how you think, your curiosity and your care for users than a perfect match. How we hire Four stages: a 30-minute call with our Talent team, a 60-minute portfolio review, a 60-minute design interview in person at our Paris office, and a closing 30-minute conversation. The portfolio review and design interview are built around your own work and how you design. Please apply with your CV and a link to your portfolio showing your latest work. title: Research Lead, Predictive Oncology
description: About Orakl Oncology At Orakl Oncology, we combine patient-derived tumor models, experimental drug screening and computational modelling to improve oncology drug development. Our research brings together functional treatment-response measurements, molecular profiles and clinical information where available, creating opportunities to investigate how experimental responses translate into patient outcomes. Our platforms are designed to help anticipate clinical trial outcomes, evaluate therapies and identify new therapeutic opportunities. Our mission is simple yet ambitious: to bring more effective treatments to patients who need them and to make drug development smarter, faster, and more personalised. We collaborate with top hospitals, research institutes, and pharmaceutical companies worldwide. Backed by leading investors, we are a fast-growing, mission-driven startup at the intersection of science and technology. About the Role We are looking for a Research Lead - Predictive Oncology, to build and lead a research programme to improve the translational capabilities of Orakl Oncology’s platform, and to provide the scientific backbone of O-Predict, Orakl’s predictive solutions. You will own O-Predict's long-term scientific roadmap, choose the questions we pursue, and lead the work needed to answer them. The opportunity combines access to Orakl's experimental and molecular data, clinical information where available, and the ability to shape future data generation with our experimental and clinical collaborators. This is a hands-on scientific leadership role . You will develop and test methods, mentor contributors, and build a coherent body of research with a recognisable scientific contribution. Publications, presentations and external collaborations will be integral outputs of that programme. You will work closely with the CTO and our Data Science, Computational Biology, experimental, product and engineering colleagues. Your research will establish which predictions are reliable, identify their limitations, and inform how O-Predict can support drug-development decisions. The role is suited to a researcher ready to take ownership of an independent programme within a collaborative company, including an emerging research leader with a strong record of original work. What You'll Do Own O-Predict's long-term research roadmap: define and maintain a 2-year scientific agenda, translated into a prioritised 12-month execution plan. Identify the key uncertainties, research hypotheses, data requirements, dependencies and resources; set milestones and explicit criteria for continuing, redirecting or stopping projects. Review priorities with the CTO as evidence and company needs evolve. Lead R&D execution: take research programmes from question formulation through method development, validation and interpretation. Coordinate agreed contributions across Data Science, Computational Biology and experimental teams, establish project ownership, run scientific reviews, resolve blockers and mentor researchers. Remain hands-on in the analyses and modelling decisions that determine scientific quality. Shape future data generation: identify the experiments, measurements and cohorts that would resolve important scientific uncertainties. Co-design these studies with experimental and clinical colleagues, prioritise them within the agreed research allocation, and use the results to test and revise your hypotheses. Advance O-Predict's predictive capabilities: investigate how drug screening, patient-derived models, molecular and clinical data can improve treatment-response and trial-outcome predictions. Assess extensions to new cohorts, indications and therapeutic settings, specifying the evidence needed before extending claims. Own the validation strategy: define relevant endpoints, external baselines and evaluation protocols. Lead independent and prospective validation plans with clinical and experimental collaborators, and document both performance and failure modes. Connect research to product development: work with product and engineering colleagues to translate promising findings into reproducible methods and clearly documented scientific requirements. Define the evidence needed for transfer into O-Predict and assess feasibility, expected value and limitations. Lead publications and scientific materials: build a publication and conference plan around the research roadmap. Lead manuscripts from analysis and figures through submission and reviewer responses, with contributions distributed across the research team. Produce abstracts, posters, talks and methods notes; provide scientific direction and review for partner evidence decks. Build substantive scientific collaborations: work directly with clinical investigators and quantitative researchers to formulate questions, co-design studies, access complementary expertise and pursue independent validation opportunities. Represent O-Predict at relevant oncology and computational conferences, present your team's research, and turn scientific discussions into joint projects and publications. Run publication governance: coordinate authorship and co-author review with hospital and pharmaceutical partners, track contractual publication and acknowledgement obligations, and align disclosure with confidentiality, patient-data permissions and intellectual-property considerations. Minimum Qualifications PhD, PharmD, MD, or MSc with an equivalent research record in a quantitative or biomedical discipline relevant to predictive oncology. Demonstrated ownership of a research programme: you have formulated a scientific agenda, prioritised competing questions and led projects from initial hypothesis to validated findings. Experience leading and mentoring scientific contributors , including coordinating work across disciplines and critically reviewing others' methods and conclusions. A strong publication record in translational oncology, computational biology, biostatistics and/or ML for health , with clear intellectual and analytical contributions. Hands-on proficiency in Python and SQL: you can work with internal data and libraries, develop and evaluate methods, and produce reproducible analyses and figures. Strong grounding in statistical inference, predictive modelling and study design; able to challenge biological assumptions and machine-learning evaluations. Excellent scientific writing and oral communication in English , including manuscripts, scientific presentations and substantive discussions with external researchers. Preferred Qualifications Experience leading R&D in a biotech, health technology or translational research setting, with responsibility for milestones and resource planning. Experience translating research methods into a predictive product or decision-support workflow. Familiarity with patient-derived models, drug sensitivity assays, clinical trial design and oncology endpoints. Experience with independent or prospective validation, multimodal data integration, survival modelling, or pharmacological modelling. Experience establishing academic or clinical collaborations and publishing with pharmaceutical partners. Familiarity with appropriate reporting standards and reproducibility practices, including protocol registration and code and data availability statements. Experience presenting research at oncology or computational conferences and maintaining an active scientific network. Who You Are A scientific owner: you turn an ambitious objective into a focused research agenda and make explicit choices about what deserves the team's time. A hands-on leader: you develop others while staying close enough to the data and code to challenge results and solve difficult problems. Rigorous and intellectually honest: you seek evidence that could disprove your hypotheses, distinguish exploratory findings from validated claims, and report limitations clearly. Curious across disciplines: you connect experimental biology, clinical questions and quantitative methods. An effective collaborator: you build productive relationships, navigate scientific disagreement and turn external discussions into research progress. Why Join Orakl Own a research programme with a clear scientific identity. Shape O-Predict's direction and build a body of work around the translation of experimental treatment responses into clinical predictions. Study a distinctive combination of data. Bring together patient-derived tumor models, functional drug screening and molecular profiles, incorporating clinical information where available. Explore questions that require these modalities to be studied together. Help decide what gets measured next. Work with experimental and clinical colleagues to design new studies that test your ideas and address the limitations of existing data. Work across disciplines every day. Develop methods alongside the scientists generating the measurements, the engineers supporting their use, and collaborators who understand the clinical questions. Build your scientific reputation. Lead original research, manuscripts and conference contributions, and develop sustained collaborations around your programme. Connect discoveries to consequential decisions. Develop and validate methods intended to inform therapy evaluation and clinical development, with a clear account of what the evidence does and does not support. Grow as a research leader. Mentor researchers and help shape the capabilities and future team needed to deliver the programme. Interview Process HR Call: Align on motivation, role scope and expectations. Scientific Deep Dive: Discuss a research programme you led: the questions you chose, your own technical contributions, validation decisions, team leadership and published outcomes. We will share a confidential scientific briefing on O-Predict's current evidence, available data and open questions so you can assess the opportunity. Research Strategy and Analysis Discussion: Using a bounded, representative evidence package, discuss research priorities and a validation plan, critique an analysis, and outline how you would communicate the findings. Meet the experimental and computational colleagues you would work with and discuss the studies you would want to pursue. Reference Call: Speak with one or two close collaborators who can assess scientific judgement, research ownership and leadership. Founder Interview: Discuss O-Predict's scientific direction, decision-making responsibilities, research resources, publication arrangements and mutual ambitions. Find Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

We are looking for a Research Lead - Predictive Oncology, to build and lead a research programme to improve the translational capabilities of Orakl Oncology’s platform, and to provide the scientific backbone of O-Predict, Orakl’s predictive solutions.

You will own O-Predict's long-term scientific roadmap, choose the questions we pursue, and lead the work needed to answer them. The opportunity combines access to Orakl's experimental and molecular data, clinical information where available, and the ability to shape future data generation with our experimental and clinical collaborators.

This is a hands-on scientific leadership role. You will develop and test methods, mentor contributors, and build a coherent body of research with a recognisable scientific contribution. Publications, presentations and external collaborations will be integral outputs of that programme.

You will work closely with the CTO and our Data Science, Computational Biology, experimental, product and engineering colleagues. Your research will establish which predictions are reliable, identify their limitations, and inform how O-Predict can support drug-development decisions.

The role is suited to a researcher ready to take ownership of an independent programme within a collaborative company, including an emerging research leader with a strong record of original work.

What You'll Do

Own O-Predict's long-term research roadmap: define and maintain a 2-year scientific agenda, translated into a prioritised 12-month execution plan. Identify the key uncertainties, research hypotheses, data requirements, dependencies and resources; set milestones and explicit criteria for continuing, redirecting or stopping projects. Review priorities with the CTO as evidence and company needs evolve.

Lead R&D execution: take research programmes from question formulation through method development, validation and interpretation. Coordinate agreed contributions across Data Science, Computational Biology and experimental teams, establish project ownership, run scientific reviews, resolve blockers and mentor researchers. Remain hands-on in the analyses and modelling decisions that determine scientific quality.

Shape future data generation: identify the experiments, measurements and cohorts that would resolve important scientific uncertainties. Co-design these studies with experimental and clinical colleagues, prioritise them within the agreed research allocation, and use the results to test and revise your hypotheses.

Advance O-Predict's predictive capabilities: investigate how drug screening, patient-derived models, molecular and clinical data can improve treatment-response and trial-outcome predictions. Assess extensions to new cohorts, indications and therapeutic settings, specifying the evidence needed before extending claims.

Own the validation strategy: define relevant endpoints, external baselines and evaluation protocols. Lead independent and prospective validation plans with clinical and experimental collaborators, and document both performance and failure modes.

Connect research to product development: work with product and engineering colleagues to translate promising findings into reproducible methods and clearly documented scientific requirements. Define the evidence needed for transfer into O-Predict and assess feasibility, expected value and limitations.

Lead publications and scientific materials: build a publication and conference plan around the research roadmap. Lead manuscripts from analysis and figures through submission and reviewer responses, with contributions distributed across the research team. Produce abstracts, posters, talks and methods notes; provide scientific direction and review for partner evidence decks.

Build substantive scientific collaborations: work directly with clinical investigators and quantitative researchers to formulate questions, co-design studies, access complementary expertise and pursue independent validation opportunities. Represent O-Predict at relevant oncology and computational conferences, present your team's research, and turn scientific discussions into joint projects and publications.

Run publication governance: coordinate authorship and co-author review with hospital and pharmaceutical partners, track contractual publication and acknowledgement obligations, and align disclosure with confidentiality, patient-data permissions and intellectual-property considerations.

Minimum Qualifications

  • PhD, PharmD, MD, or MSc with an equivalent research record in a quantitative or biomedical discipline relevant to predictive oncology.

  • Demonstrated ownership of a research programme: you have formulated a scientific agenda, prioritised competing questions and led projects from initial hypothesis to validated findings.

  • Experience leading and mentoring scientific contributors, including coordinating work across disciplines and critically reviewing others' methods and conclusions.

  • A strong publication record in translational oncology, computational biology, biostatistics and/or ML for health, with clear intellectual and analytical contributions.

  • Hands-on proficiency in Python and SQL: you can work with internal data and libraries, develop and evaluate methods, and produce reproducible analyses and figures.

  • Strong grounding in statistical inference, predictive modelling and study design; able to challenge biological assumptions and machine-learning evaluations.

  • Excellent scientific writing and oral communication in English, including manuscripts, scientific presentations and substantive discussions with external researchers.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading R&D in a biotech, health technology or translational research setting, with responsibility for milestones and resource planning.

  • Experience translating research methods into a predictive product or decision-support workflow.

  • Familiarity with patient-derived models, drug sensitivity assays, clinical trial design and oncology endpoints.

  • Experience with independent or prospective validation, multimodal data integration, survival modelling, or pharmacological modelling.

  • Experience establishing academic or clinical collaborations and publishing with pharmaceutical partners.

  • Familiarity with appropriate reporting standards and reproducibility practices, including protocol registration and code and data availability statements.

  • Experience presenting research at oncology or computational conferences and maintaining an active scientific network.

Who You Are

  • A scientific owner: you turn an ambitious objective into a focused research agenda and make explicit choices about what deserves the team's time.

  • A hands-on leader: you develop others while staying close enough to the data and code to challenge results and solve difficult problems.

  • Rigorous and intellectually honest: you seek evidence that could disprove your hypotheses, distinguish exploratory findings from validated claims, and report limitations clearly.

  • Curious across disciplines: you connect experimental biology, clinical questions and quantitative methods.

  • An effective collaborator: you build productive relationships, navigate scientific disagreement and turn external discussions into research progress.

Why Join Orakl

  • Own a research programme with a clear scientific identity. Shape O-Predict's direction and build a body of work around the translation of experimental treatment responses into clinical predictions.

  • Study a distinctive combination of data. Bring together patient-derived tumor models, functional drug screening and molecular profiles, incorporating clinical information where available. Explore questions that require these modalities to be studied together.

  • Help decide what gets measured next. Work with experimental and clinical colleagues to design new studies that test your ideas and address the limitations of existing data.

  • Work across disciplines every day. Develop methods alongside the scientists generating the measurements, the engineers supporting their use, and collaborators who understand the clinical questions.

  • Build your scientific reputation. Lead original research, manuscripts and conference contributions, and develop sustained collaborations around your programme.

  • Connect discoveries to consequential decisions. Develop and validate methods intended to inform therapy evaluation and clinical development, with a clear account of what the evidence does and does not support.

  • Grow as a research leader. Mentor researchers and help shape the capabilities and future team needed to deliver the programme.

Interview Process

  1. HR Call: Align on motivation, role scope and expectations.

  2. Scientific Deep Dive: Discuss a research programme you led: the questions you chose, your own technical contributions, validation decisions, team leadership and published outcomes. We will share a confidential scientific briefing on O-Predict's current evidence, available data and open questions so you can assess the opportunity.

  3. Research Strategy and Analysis Discussion: Using a bounded, representative evidence package, discuss research priorities and a validation plan, critique an analysis, and outline how you would communicate the findings. Meet the experimental and computational colleagues you would work with and discuss the studies you would want to pursue.

  4. Reference Call: Speak with one or two close collaborators who can assess scientific judgement, research ownership and leadership.

  5. Founder Interview: Discuss O-Predict's scientific direction, decision-making responsibilities, research resources, publication arrangements and mutual ambitions.

title: Ingénieure ou ingénieur de recherche – Captage du CO₂
description: Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne , c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable . Une école d’excellence où chacun   a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain . Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.   L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.   À Mines Saint-Étienne, nos centres de recherche sont le cœur battant de notre École. Pensés comme de véritables hubs d’innovation, nos cinq Centres de Formation et de Recherche  articulent leurs expertises autour de grands enjeux industriels, environnementaux, sociétaux et technologiques. Leur mission ? Imaginer le monde de demain en alliant excellence académique et impact concret. Vous rêvez d’une industrie propre, efficace et durable ? Le centre SPIN en fait sa priorité. Énergie, environnement, procédés industriels… on y conçoit des systèmes pour produire  mieux, avec moins. L’objectif ?  Limiter l’impact environnemental, réduire la consommation énergétique et booster l’efficacité. 🔧 Dans un monde en pleine mutation, nos équipes déploient leur créativité scientifique pour accompagner l’ industrie du futur.  Et vous, prêt·e à innover à nos côtés ? 🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous En tant qu’ Ingénieur(e), vous êtes au cœur de nos missions en recherche et innovation affecté au Centre SPIN. Au sein de ce centre, vous conjuguez passion scientifique et impact sociétal afin de contribuer à l’atteinte des objectifs de neutralité carbone de la France. Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain.

Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.

 L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.
